one_month_reasoning: No Booking earnings in the window (Q4 FY2026 results come in late February 2027); the Q4 guide was set on 2026-11-03 and the stock has drifted to $153.28 (2026-11-19, VCP Scanner). Scheduled: the December FOMC and US CPI, Thanksgiving/holiday travel reads, peers' conference remarks; unscheduled: an FTC settlement or complaint (10-Q: not agreed), the EU DSA probe, Middle East escalation or de-escalation. None has a known sign, and post-earnings drift after a mixed print (beat on bookings, weak guide) is small. So a near-symmetric lognormal from $153.28 with a +0.3% drift, at the stock's 39% annual vol over 19 trading days (sigma ~10.7%, close to the annual/3.5 = 11.1% rule).

fair_value.method: Quarterly driver build (room nights x GB per room night x take rate; adjusted EBITDA margin) valued at the horizon with P/E 14.6x on our NTM EPS (weight 0.75) and EV/EBITDA 11.85x on LTM EBITDA (0.25), less FTC/Spain liabilities; engine base horizon value $180.97.

methods.name: P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Actuals from releases (Q1 FY2025-Q3 FY2026). Q4 FY2026 = 285 x 1.035 (guide 1-3% by CFO Steenbergen; record +2.7% on levels; trimmed for October Middle East hit and Expedia's Q4 slowdown). FY2027 quarters y/y +4.5/5.5/4.5/5.5% (tough Q1/Q3 comps after +6.0%/+6.8%; easy Q2 after the Middle East hit and Q4 after +3.5%); FY2028 +5%. Real-world case: global travel grows GDP+1-2pts (CEO Fogel, JPM conf.), ~4-5% a year, plus Booking share gain; in 2026 Booking room nights grew 6.0% YTD vs UN Tourism's 1-2% arrivals forecast, i.e. ~4pts of outgrowth in a weak year; we take ~1pt less outgrowth than 2026 as AI channels and Middle East persist. Alternatives: (a) guide-record path ~+4.75% Q4 and 6% 2027; (b) consensus 2027 revenue +10.6% GAAP (~+7.9% ex-FTC) implying ~6% RN; (c) UN Tourism 1-2% + 2026 outgrowth 4.5pts = 5.5-6.5%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: RN 6% in 2027-28 (consensus-like) adds ~2% to the research target (12m); a 2027 recession (Kalshi 21.5%) would take RN to ~0-1%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Actual adjusted EBITDA / adjusted revenue (SBC expensed). Q4 FY2026 = Q4 FY2025 34.57% - 0.5pt for the higher planned Q4 investments the CFO named (guide 'about flat' EBITDA on +0-2% revenue implies -0.3 to -0.6pt). FY2027 and FY2028 +0.3pt y/y each quarter: CFO says $650M run-rate transformation savings in 2027 (each $100M ~0.3pt of revenue) but FY2026's margin plan went +50bp -> stable as investments absorbed savings (Earnings Whispers), and B2B affiliate marketing deleverages; we credit ~$100M net a year. Alternatives: flat margin (FY2026 outcome), +0.5pt (FY2026 initial plan), consensus 2027 EPS +17.5% (implies ~+0.5-1pt with buybacks).
inputs_detail.variant_view: +0.5pt a year (initial FY2026 plan) adds ~1% to the research target (12m); flat margin takes ~1% off.

inputs_detail.derivation: Peer median NTM P/E of EXPE 15.3x and ABNB 29.7x = 22.5x; own NTM P/E = 157.53 / ~12.0 (consensus FY2026 10.42 and FY2027 12.23 time-weighted over Nov 2026-Nov 2027) = 13.1x; exit = 22.5 x (13.1/22.5)^0.8 = 14.6x. Base-rate check: Booking's 10-year forward P/E lows were 15-16x (eToro) and TTM P/E has not held below ~16-18x outside 2008 (VCP Scanner history); 14.6x keeps most of today's AI-disruption discount. Alternatives: 3-peer median incl. UBER (17.2x -> 13.8x exit); own multiple unchanged 13.1x; historical trough 15-16x.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Exit at 13.1x (no shrink) takes ~-7% off the P/E leg; at the 16x historical trough +10%.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: LTM adjusted EBITDA at the horizon x 11.85x (EXPE 9.9x shrunk from own 12.4x), less net debt and adjustments

inputs_detail.derivation: EXPE trailing 9.9x (only genuine peer with the figure); own TTM EV/EBITDA = (157.53 x 743.7 + 4,247) / 9,813 = 12.4x; exit = 9.9 x (12.4/9.9)^0.8 = 11.85x on LTM EBITDA at the horizon.

downside.story: P10: a 2027 US/European recession (Kalshi 21.5% for 2027) plus persisting Middle East disruption takes room nights ~4.5% below base (growth ~0-1%), ADR/FX -1.5%, margin -1.5pts as marketing deleverages; AI-agent disintermediation fear compresses P/E to ~11x (below the 2008/2020 trough area)

reasoning: Base rates first: Booking has beaten 4 of its last 5 room-night guides (median +2.7% on levels) and all 5 revenue and EBITDA guides (median +3.0% and +5.8%), but its first FY2026 annual guide ('low double digits' revenue, mid-teens EPS) was cut to high single digits, so the beat habit is quarterly sandbagging, not annual. The Q4 FY2026 guide (RN +1-3%) is the weakest in years; Expedia's Q4 bookings guide (+3.3-5.2% after +11%) and UN Tourism's cut to 1-2% arrivals growth show an industry slowdown from the Middle East conflict and airfares, not a Booking-specific break. Macro odds: Kalshi prices a 2027 US recession at ~21.5%; Polymarket's 2026 market is ~2% (oddpool's 37% looks stale). Valuation history: the stock sits at ~13x NTM consensus EPS, below its decade forward-P/E lows of 15-16x (eToro) and a TTM ~16x vs a 5-year median ~29x (VCP Scanner), after a ~34% peak-to-trough drawdown (TIKR) and -20% over a year. Model: quarterly room nights x GB/RN x take, margins from the adjusted EBITDA margin with a +0.3pt/yr step from the $650M savings net of investment; FY2027 revenue ~1pt below consensus ex-FTC; our FY2027 EPS is ~$11.5 vs StockAnalysis $12.23 (-6%): about 1pt from revenue, ~2pts from net interest at the 8.5% Q3 run-rate on net debt that rises as returns run at 30% of revenue, ~2pts from buybacks at -5% a year vs the -7.5% Q3 pace, and the rest from a margin step (+0.3pt) below the +0.5pt FY2026 plan. Horizon P/E per the k=0.8 rule on a 2-peer median, EV/EBITDA cross-check. Downside (P10) combines recession-type volumes with a de-rating to ~11x; upside (P90) a guide beat plus partial re-rating to ~17.6x. Research limited: SEC EDGAR refused the generic curl agent, so filings were read with WebFetch; X/Twitter not tried.

model_inputs.structure_note: Single-segment marketplace (Booking reports one segment; B2B to be shown separately from 2027). Quarterly driver build: adjusted revenue = room nights x gross bookings per room night x take rate; EBIT = revenue x (adjusted EBITDA margin - D&A 2.1%). EBIT is on Booking's adjusted basis, which expenses SBC (CFO: 'fully loaded expense base, including stock-based compensation') and excludes the Q3 2026 FTC matter ($1.0B), transformation costs and FX/equity marks; the FTC and Spain liabilities enter as equity adjustments instead. Value is carried by the P/E leg (75%) on our NTM EPS at the horizon (Q4 FY2027-Q3 FY2028) and an EV/EBITDA cross-check (25%) on LTM EBITDA; no DCF (policy), no SOTP (single segment, no disclosed split).
model_inputs.gap_note: Peer set is 2 genuine peers (EXPE, ABNB): UBER is in the run's table but its business matches 0% of Booking's revenue, so it is excluded from the median (segment-only rule); Trip.com and MakeMyTrip are excluded by the country-distortion rule. A 2-peer median is fragile: on UBER-included 3-peer median (17.2x) the exit P/E would be ~13.8x (-5%). Peer EPS bases differ: EXPE consensus adjusted EPS adds back SBC, ABNB is near-GAAP, Booking's adjusted EPS expenses SBC; on one SBC-costed basis the peer median would be higher, so the k=0.8 exit is conservative. Share count -5%/yr is a judgment from FCF ~$9B/yr less ~$1.3B dividends at ~$160-180/share less ~0.5% SBC dilution; no shares.buyback reprice schedule given. Interest 8.5% on net debt is the Q3 2026 net interest run-rate ((311-221) x 4 / 4,247). Financing: none probable (>20%); the $2.0B notes due within 12 months are expected to be refinanced (no change to net debt). Lane: base-rates.
